messages:
Maya: paging: multiple runtime pods started OOM'ing on gpu-allocs, high paging observed, impacting hosted inference. oncall-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-03-15-GPU-PAGE. Triggering channel and pager. Omar: I'm on it, joining. brief summary? Maya: backend latency spikes ~300ms -> 2s for some chat requests, customers reporting 502 and timeouts. Root cause looks like GPU memory fragmentation leading to kernel-level paging. ops-bot: Prod alert: runtime-gpu-alloc OOM rate increased 18x since 08:12 UTC. nodes: gpunode-23,gpunode-24,gpunode-39. Tess: sharing quick timeline below — need someone to confirm customer impact window and if any Dedicated customers hit error rate >5% Maya: Timeline (raw): 08:09 - first slow request spike 08:11 - runtime OOM on gpunode-23, POD runtime-v2-7 restarted 08:12 - pager fires; cascading restarts on gpunode-24 08:13 - autoscaler kicks, new pods scheduled but also OOM 08:18 - we applied temporary traffic routing to low-cost region 08:20 - manual batch-size cap applied to inference route, partial recovery 08:25 - ops toggled kv-cache=off for heavy routes (A/B) 08:30 - observed error rates falling, but intermittent 502s continue Omar: attaching snippet from node dmesg and nvidia-smi output (redacted): ```dmesg | tail -n 40
[  467.123456] Out of memory: Killed process 12345 (runtime) total-vm:2756480kB, anon-rss:2048000kB
[  467.123789] GPU memory allocation failed: fragment alloc ropage
``` ```nvidia-smi --query-compute-apps=pid,used_memory,gpu_uuid --format=csv
pid, used_memory [MiB], gpu_uuid
12345, 15360, GPU-a1b2c3
12367, 14000, GPU-a1b2c3
``` Omar: note memory per-process is high and there are many small allocations. Hypothesis A: KV cache fragmentation + batch-size spikes -> kernel cannot satisfy contiguous allocation -> OOM. Hypothesis B: a regression in allocator path after recent runtime change that increased slab churn. Tess: I'm running a heap profile capture on the runtime process (sampling) and will drop logs to the incident bucket once ready. Lin: oncall is reducing max concurrency and forcing streaming route to prefer smaller seq-length. Command used: ```kubectl set env deployment/runtime --containers=runtime MAX_BATCH_SIZE=8 --record``` Lin: also applied `RUNTIME_KV_CACHE_ENABLED=false` on route heavy-chat-*. Maya: recorded customer impact: two mid-market customers saw request failure rate ~7% during 08:11-08:22, small startups hit latency but mostly retry succeeded. Ops: nodes with highest frag: gpunode-23 had 78% mem fragmentation score (node exporter metric gpu_mem_frag_ratio=0.78). Omar: can you paste the metrics graph link? Tess: https://grafana.redwood/prod/d/allocs/gpu-fragmentation?orgId=1&from=1678894200000&to=1678894380000 Omar: thanks. I see pattern of slowly rising fragmentation across 6 hours then sharp spike at 08:10. That rules in long-running fragmentation. Maya: immediate mitigations applied and helped: - cap batch size to 8 - disable kv cache on heavy routes - temporarily route new sessions to different region - increase eviction aggressiveness in runtime's slab allocator to free small objects faster Omar: actionable checklist for responders: 1) collect full node dmesg + kernel logs 2) gcore or heap profile for runtime process 3) gather nvidia-smi sample series from last 2 hours 4) run allocator debug to dump slab hist 5) check recent runtime commits touching alloc/kvcache (PRs #4021, #4033) Tess: I grabbed a gcore (PID 12345) and pushed to s3://redwood-incidents/INC-2026-03-15/gcore-12345.tar.gz (link in private). Also uploaded pprof profile: s3://.../pprof-08-15.pb.gz Lin: I'm going to run a controlled test on staging reproducer: heavy KV-backed requests with long prefix + repeated small updates to force fragmentation. Omar: noted. For live mitigation, is it safe to keep kv-cache off? Maya: costly but acceptable short term; might increase token cost but reduces OOM risk. Also need to communicate to support. Tess: temporary fix notes: - rollback runtime allocator change from PR #4033 on canary - if fragmentation persists, schedule node restart and drain at 30-min intervals to defragment GPU memory - longer term: implement buddy allocator or compaction hook for gpu pages Omar: hypothesis tracking: Hypothesis A (kv-cache fragmentation) -> supported by nvidia-smi gaps + grafana trend -> status: likely Tess: Hypothesis B (allocator regression) -> next: bisect PRs between 4020..4040 to see regression introduction -> status: investigating Maya: please prepare customer impact blurb for public incident timeline: "From ~08:11 to 08:22 UTC some inference requests returned errors or experienced increased latency due to GPU memory pressure. We applied mitigations (batch caps, kv cache toggle, routing) and recovered by ~08:30 UTC. Working on root cause and will share postmortem." Lin: putting postmortem draft in /incidents/INC-2026-03-15/draft.md Omar: assigning followups: - Tess: collect and attach full allocator dumps + timeline (owner) - Lin: reproduce in staging and test allocator changes (owner) - Maya: coordinate customer comms and legal notifications if needed (owner) - Eng-runtime: schedule defrag feature planning (group) ops-bot: Action taken: MAX_BATCH_SIZE=8 applied to deployment/runtime at 08:20 UTC; KV cache disabled on route heavy-chat at 08:25 UTC oncall-bot: Pager cleared by Omar at 08:40 UTC Maya: marking this thread as the primary coordination thread for RCA; drop all artifacts links here. Also add any new hypotheses as they emerge. Omar: I'll start the PR bisect tomorrow morning and share a timeline of candidate commits. Tess: uploading allocator dump now, will DM link. quick note: when re-enabling kv-cache, do a canary on 2 pods only and watch gpu_mem_frag_ratio. Lin: agreed. Maya: thanks all. closing live coordination; will reconvene at 11:00 UTC for postmortem sync. :thumbsup:
